newsitem.title: GERMANY: Junk mail clogs German e-mail service.
newsitem.headline: Junk mail clogs German e-mail service.

text.p: Customers of Deutsche Telekom's online service T-Online complained over the weekend of a blackout in the company's electronic mail services, a company spokesman said on Sunday.
Some T-Online users complained that they had not been able to send or receive electronic mail for the past three days.

A Telekom spokesman acknowleged that there have been difficulties accessing the service, Germany's largest online service, for the past few days because an unsual increase in the amount of junk e-mail was tying up traffic.
The increasing use of e-mail by a broad public has given rise to companies that offer to send unsolicited electronic advertising via e-mail to millions of unsuspecting Internet surfers.

A highly improper activity in the world of Internet ethics, such "spamming" of cybernauts is frowned upon. Some online services such as America Online of the United States have blocked offenders from accessing their services.
Deutsche Telekom said it was working on the problem.
